dependencies.reason: runs its label rules again after the session and extends its dry run; af-impl's closing of items is the base the reconcile mode builds on

tasks.title: Schedule the reconcile step and start its session with the issues it may adopt
steps: Add the scheduling table, the restart cases, the selection table and the session checks as tests and confirm they fail; teach the fake claude a reconcile script: write labels, close issues, write the report, or misbehave
Add the flag --reconcile-every with its SPECRUN_RECONCILE_EVERY default: an integer, default 5, 0 meaning only the reconcile at the end; refuse a negative number or a non-integer as a usage error

Keep in the state file the number of packages landed since the last reconcile. When it reaches the flag's value, and when every package is done and a package landed since the last reconcile or the ledger holds no reconcile, the next step is a reconcile; a reconcile recorded as running at start is run again

At the start of a reconcile list the open issues, following an incomplete listing to its end, and select those with no label starting af: whose title starts with a package's directory name and a colon, for the packages under the spec root and its archive; write them as a JSON array of number, title, url and package to <step>-adopt.json in the log directory

Start the session with the prompt `/af-impl --reconcile <adopt file> --report <log dir>/<step>-report.md` and everything else as for a package: the flags, the process group, the stream files and the stall rule

After the session check that the base branch is checked out, the tree is clean and HEAD is the commit it was; a failure stops the loop with the check as the reason and applies no rule. A report file that does not exist is the warning reconcile_report_missing

tasks.title: Apply the rules after the session and report the reconcile
steps: Add the unsettled adoption, the deviation table, the ledger line and the dry run as tests and confirm they fail
Add the rule adoption-unsettled: an issue of the adopt file that is still open with no kind label gets af:deviation and af:from-<NN> of the package its title names, with a comment

Add the rules deviation-accepted and deviation-rejected over the open issues labelled af:deviation: accepted and not rejected is closed with a comment naming the first docs/adr path in its body, or saying none is cited; rejected and not accepted loses af:deviation and af:rejected and gains af:defect and af:severity-correctness, with a comment; both labels is left alone with the warning deviation_conflict

Then apply incomplete-labels and awaits-finished to every open af: issue. Every change carries a comment with its rule and the commit of the base branch, each rule is a function to a list of changes like the earlier ones, and a forge failure stops the loop

Write the ledger line with kind reconcile, outcome reconciled and the numbers adopted, closed and settled; put the open deviations with neither label, oldest first, in result.open_deviations and print them on stderr; return the count of packages since the last reconcile to 0
Under --dry-run report a due reconcile as the next step, the selection as result.would_adopt and the deviation changes in result.would_change, writing no file and nothing to the forge

Document the reconcile in docs/specrun.md: when it runs, the adopt file and the report, the checks, each rule, the ledger line, and how a person settles a deviation with af:accepted or af:rejected; add the flag and its variable to docs/configuration.md

tasks.title: Give af-impl its reconcile mode
steps: Extend the fake session's reconcile script and the end-to-end test so that the prompt specrun sends is the one the skill documents, and confirm the test fails before the prompt is final

Add skills/af-impl/references/reconcile.md and link it from SKILL.md: `/af-impl --reconcile <adopt file> --report <report file>` implements no package; it reads the two paths from its arguments and stops with a report when either is missing

Adopting, in that file: for each issue of the adopt file read its body, which says what is missing, why, the evidence and what closes it; assign its kind, af:from-<NN>, af:awaits-<NN> when it awaits a package and a severity when it is a defect; add the labels with `issue <ref> --edit --add-label` and a comment saying the issue was adopted and why it got that kind; label an issue whose kind the body does not settle af:deviation; touch no issue that is not in the file and carries no af: label

Checking closing conditions, in that file: list every open af:* issue; for each decide whether the condition in 'What closes it' holds on the base branch; close those that hold with `issue <ref> --close --body`, the comment giving the evidence as file and line and a test; change no code, create no branch and commit nothing

The report, in that file: Markdown written to the report path, listing what was adopted with the kind given, what was closed with its evidence, and the rest by kind and severity, deviations oldest first

In SKILL.md name the mode in the argument hint and in §1, and extend the last rule of *Never*: in a reconcile af-impl may label the issues of the adopt file; keep the rendered body under the ceiling `make skills-check` enforces
